root_cause.text: The original code used pskb_pull and pskb_trim on cloned/coalesced skbs from the TCP stream parser, which can cause the offset between skb->data and skb->head to exceed the 16-bit network_header field, leading to header corruption and packet drops, and also introduces unaligned access penalties.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states: "Using pskb_pull with large offsets on coalesced skbs causes skb->data - skb->head to exceed the u16 storage of skb->network_header. This causes skb_reset_network_header to fail on the inner decapsulated packet, resulting in packet drops." The patch replaces the pskb_pull/pskb_trim approach with allocation of a new skb and skb_copy_bits.

candidates.rationale: Calling pskb_pull on a cloned/coalesced skb can cause the offset between skb->data and skb->head to exceed the 16-bit network_header field, corrupting packet headers.
Calling pskb_trim on a cloned/coalesced skb can similarly corrupt the network header offset and introduce unaligned access penalties.
pskb_may_pull is used after pskb_pull and pskb_trim; it may interact unsafely with the already modified skb, contributing to header corruption.
skb_push after manipulation of data offset can cause the network header offset to become invalid, especially on cloned/coalesced skbs.
This statement computes the trim length based on the strp message; if the message offset causes pskb_trim to create an invalid offset, it is part of the vulnerable flow.
This statement computes the pull offset from the strp message; an incorrect offset passed to pskb_pull directly contributes to header corruption.
